assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Create one atlas containing separate original picture assets for a first-grade lesson.
Use 2 equal rows and 3 equal columns, with one fully visible object centered in each occupied cell. Keep wide empty margins around every object and between cells. No crossing cell boundaries, touching subjects, dividers, frames, text, letters, numbers, labels, logos or watermarks. Leave unused cells empty. Use true transparent alpha for the background, including the margins. Do not draw a checkerboard.

Keep a consistent matte gouache and fine paper grain, with clean cut-paper contours. Use deep pine green, warm cream, apricot and persimmon as accents when appropriate. Keep the objects immediately recognizable and retain the real or lesson-specific colors and details in the descriptions. An object used for counting appears exactly once in its own cell.

Cell positions, in reading order:
Row 1, column 1: Two tiny cream panels inside one picture, spaced left to right. The same domestic chicken at two ages, small yellow chick at left and taller cream juvenile hen at right. In both it stands left-facing and has one distinct identical muted rusty spot near the base of the visible wing. Only one chicken in each phase. Keep a clear gap and strong contrasting silhouettes.
Row 1, column 2: Two tiny cream panels inside one picture, spaced left to right. The same tan dog at two ages, small puppy at left and larger adult at right. Same white forehead stripe and chest blaze, same left-facing quiet stance. Exactly one dog per phase. Strong simple silhouettes.
Row 1, column 3: Full side view of one adult russet hen and one tiny pale yellow newly hatched chick standing distinctly beside it and one empty split eggshell, both birds on one shared short ground line. Natural two legs per animal, clear beaks. This is one adult and its offspring together.
Row 2, column 1: One short-haired ginger-and-cream adult domestic cat lying calmly beside one tiny ginger-and-cream kitten in the same image. Clearly two separate bodies, complete silhouettes, natural legs and tails, a large size difference, both face left.
Row 2, column 2: One simple apricot glass play marble with a nearly blank pale cream center and thin dark pine rim. Round, with only subtle sheen and no surrounding object. Designed as a projectile for a moving illustration overlay.
Row 2, column 3: One wide 4:3 scene inside this cell. A child sitting an arm’s length away from an aquarium, hands resting in their own lap, with an adult calmly seated beside them. One small orange fish visibly in clear water inside the tank, closed lid, both people quietly look at it. Open notebook on a side table has a single unlabelled fish sketch. No touching, feeding, reaching or clutter. Distinct clear silhouettes and safe distance.

No dividers or frames between atlas cells. The tiny paired backgrounds inside the first two cell illustrations are intentional. The family scene is its own landscape rectangle with transparent space around it. Keep every colored pixel inside its own cell with at least 9 percent transparent padding on every side, preserve true alpha zero in the surrounding margins, no shadow or halo. Use the maximum available resolution for a landscape atlas.
